title: Zayd ibn Thabit
hookLine: the young scribe of revelation who learned new scripts, then gathered the Qur'an

lines: A BOARD AND A POT OF INK.
cards: A board, and a pot of ink. That's what the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, calls for when a new verse comes. Bring Zayd, he says, and tell him to bring the board and the inkwell.
A young man from Medina arrives and sits down to write. Halfway through, a blind companion speaks up from the room, and what happens next changes the words on the board while the ink is still wet.
Today: the young man holding the pen.

teach.b: Zayd ibn Thabit was one of the Ansar, and he wrote down revelation for the Prophet. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps the scene from the hook.

A verse came saying that believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive in God's way. Zayd wrote it. Then Ibn Umm Maktum, who was blind, spoke: Messenger of God, if I were able, I would go out too.

teach.h: EXCEPT THOSE WHO HAVE A DISABILITY.
teach.b: And before the writing was finished, a few more words came down: except those who have a disability. Zayd added them. The pen was there while the text was still arriving.
A second report, which Bukhari mentions, tells that the Prophet asked Zayd to learn the writing of the Jews of Medina, so he could write the Prophet's letters and read the ones that came back.
Zayd learned it; tradition says he picked it up quickly. So the young scribe became a translator too. Then, years later, comes the task you may remember from Hafsah's day.
When Abu Bakr decided to gather the Qur'an into written sheets, he chose Zayd, and Bukhari keeps his reason.

teach.h: YOU ARE A WISE YOUNG MAN.
teach.b: You are a wise young man, Abu Bakr told him. We do not suspect you. And you used to write the revelation for the Messenger of God.
That one sentence is a whole job description.

And practiced, because he had been at the board with the ink pot all along. Skills learned in small, ordinary moments, one verse at a time, one new alphabet at a time, became the thing the community leaned on.

how: Muslims remember Zayd ibn Thabit as a scribe of revelation and the one who gathered the Qur'an into sheets under Abu Bakr, from the reports in Sahih al-Bukhari.

o: a young scribe who wrote down the revelation
a merchant who sold ink and boards in Medina
the blind companion who spoke up in the room

s: Zayd only wrote the Qur'an down after the Prophet died
he wrote revelation for the Prophet while it was coming, at the board with the inkwell.
words were added to a verse while Zayd was still writing it
after Ibn Umm Maktum spoke, 'except those who have a disability' came down, and Zayd added it.
Abu Bakr chose Zayd because he was the oldest companion
Abu Bakr called him a wise young man whom they trusted, who used to write the revelation.

games.q: you are Zayd, writing a new verse on the board. a blind companion says he would go out too, if he were able. what happens?
o: you finish the verse as it was.
more words come down, and you add them.
you stop writing until he leaves.
games.why: Bukhari says 'except those who have a disability' was revealed, and Zayd added it while writing.

practice: Think of one small thing you've been meaning to learn, a few letters of the Arabic alphabet, a knot, a recipe, a phrase in a neighbor's language, and choose a piece small enough to start.
Picture yourself as a beginner, slow and clumsy, and let that be fine. If you pray, you can ask that what you learn be useful to someone.

wordCard.voice: Zayd, the young scribe who wrote down revelation, learned a new script for the Prophet's letters, and was chosen by Abu Bakr to gather the Qur'an. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'scribe', one who writes; the role Zayd held for the revelation.

carryVoice: Your line: the young scribe. He was at the board long before the big task came. See you tomorrow.
